---
title: "Analyze Palace adaptive refinement"
description: "Read marked elements, refinement response, energy-indicator coverage and capacitance-matrix stability from a retained Palace result."
scgsim-kind: "api"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/amr-analysis"
---

`analyze_amr(result, reference=None)` turns retained Palace adaptive mesh
refinement (AMR) evidence into a detached `PalaceAmrAnalysis`. It reports what
the solver marked and how the mesh and capacitance matrix changed between
available transitions. Display it with the public
`show_amr_analysis(analysis)` function and reuse the same object in a benchmark.
The input is either a strictly resolved Palace result or an existing partial
trust report; the function does not accept a raw path that could bypass those
result-reading contracts.

This is an offline analysis of a returned result. It does not launch Palace,
read a live simulation object, or infer missing observations. Missing passes,
gaps, and zero denominators remain explicit; derived metrics are unavailable
when their required observations are absent or invalid. Missing observations
are never filled with zero or substituted with a proxy.

The native `Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptDiagnostics` output is opt-in and
defaults to `false`. Request it when preparing the Palace input with
`set_numerical(save_adapt_diagnostics=True)`; the selected native Palace build
must support this option. For nonconformal AMR, `amr_nc_levels=1` writes the
native `MaxNCLevels` setting as `1`. Electrostatic studies may independently
request field output with `set_electrostatic(save_fields=1)` when their study
needs it; saved field or ParaView data is not a prerequisite for this AMR
analysis. Diagnostics are written under `<Problem.Output>/amr-diagnostics`,
and their manifest inventory includes the diagnostic meshes. They add storage
and I/O even when `SaveAdaptMesh` is false. SCGSim follows the returned
manifest's paths and binds its declared files through the receipt; it does not
guess paths from directory contents. The analysis itself consumes only a
returned result and does not execute the solver.

## Read the refinement indicators

For each available transition from pass $k$ to pass $k+1$, the analysis
distinguishes the native marked-element count from the computed coverage of
the squared error indicator:

$$
f_{\mathrm{marked}} = \frac{|M|}{N_{\mathrm{before}}},\qquad
c_{\eta^2} = \frac{\sum_{e\in M}\eta_e^2}{\sum_{e}\eta_e^2}.
$$

Here, $M$ is the set of marked elements, $N_{\mathrm{before}}$ is the number
of elements before refinement, and $\eta_e$ is the native element error
indicator. The marked fraction counts cells. The squared-indicator coverage
is computed from the retained native indicator squares over marked and all
cells. It is actual indicator coverage, distinct from the requested theta
fraction; it is not a percentage of cells or a measured solution error.

The transition also reports the number of actual refined parents $|P|$,
refinement closure $|P|/|M|$, extra parents $|P\setminus M|$, and element
count amplification $(N_{\mathrm{after}}-N_{\mathrm{before}})/|M|$. Closure
describes how much the mesh operation expanded the marked set; high closure
does not by itself show that refinement was wasteful or unnecessary. Actual
parent counts are required for these quantities. When the source does not
preserve them, the corresponding measures are unavailable rather than
estimated from cell counts.

True degree-of-freedom growth is reported as
$D_{\mathrm{after}}/D_{\mathrm{before}}$, alongside the degree-of-freedom
increase. This is distinct from cell-count amplification: the two can differ
as the finite-element space changes. If either degree-of-freedom count or the
denominator is unavailable, growth is unavailable.

The native energy-normalized ZZ indicator is retained as its own quantity.
For terminal sample $n$, its integrated flux discrepancy is scaled by
$\sqrt{0.5/E_{\mathrm{total}}}$ when total field energy is positive, and by
$1$ otherwise, giving $\eta_{Kn}$. Palace combines the terminal samples at
each element by root mean square and then takes the global norm:

$$
\eta_K=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{samples}}}\sum_n\eta_{Kn}^2},\qquad
\mathrm{indicator\_norm}=\sqrt{\sum_K\eta_K^2}.
$$

This is an energy-normalized flux-recovery estimate, not a capacitance percent
error or an accuracy reference. Read it alongside the main and recovery
linear-solve statuses. Driver completion is a control-flow result and does
not mean either solve converged; a capacitance matrix written by a
nonconverged solve remains an observation with its solve status attached. See
the Palace [native AMR diagnostics contract](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/palace/blob/642188ea0377c41523a6c5af710db1eb80fd6368/docs/src/features/amr_diagnostics.md)
for the producer's retained evidence and normalization.

## Compare capacitance matrices

For adjacent available passes, the analysis reports the relative Frobenius
change

$$
\frac{\|C_k-C_{k-1}\|_F}{\|C_k\|_F}
$$

and the elementwise absolute difference matrix $|C_k-C_{k-1}|$ in farads.
Raw capacitance matrices and per-terminal linear-solve state remain visible,
including when a solve did not converge. Only derived comparisons that lack
valid inputs are unavailable. A zero denominator makes the relative
Frobenius metric unavailable; the absolute entry-difference matrix can still
be reported. Missing, failed, unconverged, or non-adjacent passes make the
derived adjacent comparison unavailable. The analysis does not bridge a gap
or treat failure as a zero matrix.

An optional `CapacitanceReference` supplies a reference capacitance matrix,
terminal identities, units, and source description. Its `values` are a square
matrix in `terminal_ids` order; the immutable reference also retains `units`
and `source`. Terminal IDs must be the exact
`net_id` values from `palace_index_map.json` entries whose `section` is
`Boundaries.Terminal` (the source-conductor net IDs), not
terminal names or display labels. Matrix axes follow sorted native-index
order. When explicitly provided,
each comparable pass can report the relative Frobenius error
$\|C_k-C_{\mathrm{ref}}\|_F/\|C_{\mathrm{ref}}\|_F$. Terminal identities
must be aligned and units must agree before comparison; incompatible or
incomplete reference data remains unavailable with its reason. A reference
comparison is only as meaningful as the independently established source and
model behind that reference. The tool does not create synthetic truth data or
choose an acceptance threshold.

Without a reference, the sequence can describe whether the matrix changed
between recorded passes. It cannot establish absolute accuracy or claim an
accuracy advantage over another solver or model.

## Offline use

Resolve a returned package first, then analyze and display the detached result.
To inspect partial evidence, pass an existing trust report produced by the
inspection path. The example uses the strict resolved-result path:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.palace import (
    CapacitanceReference,
    analyze_amr,
    resolve_palace_result,
    show_amr_analysis,
)

returned_run_dir = Path(".artifacts/returned-palace")
expected_id = Path(".artifacts/palace-preparation-handoff-id.txt").read_text(
    encoding="utf-8"
).strip()
resolved = resolve_palace_result(
    returned_run_dir, expected_handoff_id=expected_id
)
analysis = analyze_amr(resolved, reference=None)
show_amr_analysis(analysis, theme="dark")
benchmark = resolved.show_simulation_benchmark(amr_analysis=analysis)
```

Pass that same `analysis` object to both presentation and benchmark so the
figures and benchmark use one interpretation of the retained evidence. The
benchmark does not rerun the analysis or invoke Palace. To compare with an
explicit reference, construct a `CapacitanceReference` from an independently
established matrix and its terminal identities, units, and source, then pass
it through `reference=`. A resolved result also provides
`resolved.show_amr_analysis(reference=reference, theme="dark")` as a combined
analysis and display convenience.

Each reported scalar is an `AmrMetric`: its `value` may be unavailable, and
its `availability`, `reason`, and `units` explain that state. Pass records
identify the native iteration and evidence source, preserve the extracted
capacitance matrix and terminal order, and retain the native ZZ norm and any
reference-capacitance comparison. `CapacitanceComparison` keeps the normalized
Frobenius change separate from `absolute_delta_f`, whose matrix value contains
elementwise differences in farads and whose terminal IDs identify its row and
column order. Transition records identify their before/after iterations and
retain the marked fraction, squared indicator coverage, closure measures,
cell amplification, degree-of-freedom growth ratio and increase, adjacent
capacitance comparison, and availability reason. The analysis also keeps
problem, run status, integrity, pass and
transition records, and the optional reference together.
`analysis.to_payload()` returns the machine-readable boundary with top-level
`run_dir`, `problem`, `run_status`, `integrity`, `passes`, `transitions`,
`reference`, `diagnostics_reason`, and `diagnostic_missing_files` fields.
The last two fields identify unavailable or incomplete native diagnostics.
Raw pass matrices and per-terminal solve validity remain
present in this payload, including when a derived comparison is unavailable.
For standard JSON, nonfinite observations are encoded as the explicit strings
`NaN`, `Infinity`, or `-Infinity`; the Python analysis retains the raw values.
Each pass also retains optional source-snapshot degree of freedom count, mesh
element count, cumulative elapsed seconds, and peak node memory in megabytes;
these are observed values, not estimates. Benchmark pass-cost records identify
`pass_index`, source, and native iteration. They report per-pass elapsed time
only when the native iterations establish it; when iterations are missing or
unknown, per-pass elapsed time and its reason remain unavailable. Cumulative
elapsed time remains visible, and a multi-step cumulative difference is not
presented as one pass duration. Transition observations retain compact raw
counts, squared-indicator sums, native IDs, and source, without embedding the
full element identity sets in the payload. Together these observations support
work-precision plots from the same analysis payload.

## Interpretation limits

Use marked fraction, indicator coverage, closure, mesh growth, degrees of
freedom, native indicator, and matrix changes as separate observations. None
is a universal mesh-adequacy threshold. Adjacent matrix stability without an
independent reference cannot establish accuracy; an independent reference
comparison does not turn the reference into a universal truth for other
models or settings.
